content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the four levels of protein structure
Explain how different bonds contribute to protein structure
Understand the relationship between structure and function
Explain what happens when proteins denature

Proteins have complex three-dimensional shapes that determine their functions. The structure of proteins is organised into four levels: primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary. Each level builds on the previous one to create the final functional protein.

Primary structure only involves peptide bonds
Only proteins with multiple polypeptide chains
Denaturation breaks bonds maintaining shape, not peptide bonds
Tertiary: overall 3D shape (disulfide, ionic, H-bonds, hydrophobic)
Globular proteins: spherical, soluble, metabolic functions
Fibrous proteins: long, insoluble, structural functions
Denaturation: loss of shape and function due to heat, pH, etc.
Structure determines function at all levels
